scope: Major outpatient diagnosis families and overlapping presentations; not an exhaustive DSM catalog

families.name: Depressive disorders
families.age: Adult core; use youth-specific treatment for minors
families.context: MDD and persistent depressive presentations: target participation, connection and agency as well as symptoms. Clarify history of mood elevation.
families.caution: Assess suicide risk and severe impairment. Possible mania, psychotic depression or inability to care for basic needs changes the care pathway.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Return to meaningful activity
targets.need: Withdrawal and loss of meaningful routines
targets.goal: Rebuild participation in activities the client values.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] personally meaningful activities per [week], from baseline [baseline], recording what helped or blocked participation.
targets.intervention: Use collaborative behavioral activation: map avoidance, choose manageable activities, schedule practice and review reinforcement and barriers.
targets.measure: Weekly activity frequency, completion with supports, and client-rated meaning or mastery.

targets.label: Reduce self-critical shutdown
targets.need: Self-criticism interrupts action and problem solving
targets.goal: Respond to setbacks with greater flexibility and self-respect.
targets.objective: By [date], use an agreed alternative response to self-critical thoughts in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], and take one chosen next step.
targets.intervention: Use CBT to examine specific predictions and self-evaluations; practice balanced responses, behavioral experiments and problem solving.
targets.measure: Self-critical shutdown frequency; use of an alternative response; ability to resume a valued task.

targets.label: Rebuild connection
targets.need: Isolation and loss of trusted support
targets.goal: Increase chosen, supportive contact without overwhelming the client.
targets.objective: By [date], initiate or accept [target] preferred supportive contacts per [week], from [baseline], with agreed access supports.
targets.intervention: Use behavioral activation or interpersonal work to identify safe relationships, communication barriers and realistic invitations.
targets.measure: Chosen contact frequency, connection rating, and quality of support rather than contact count alone.

families.name: Bipolar and related disorders
families.age: Adults; youth care needs a specialist pathway
families.context: Psychotherapy supports recovery and relapse prevention alongside psychiatric care. Clarify episode status first.
families.caution: Suspected mania, mixed symptoms, major sleep reduction with activation, or severe depression requires prompt psychiatric assessment; this is not a medication plan.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Protect rhythm and functioning
targets.need: Irregular routines and sleep precede loss of stability
targets.goal: Maintain routines that support personally meaningful functioning.
targets.objective: By [date], follow the agreed daily rhythm on [target] days per [week], from [baseline], while tracking sleep and activation.
targets.intervention: Provide bipolar-specific psychoeducation; collaboratively map routines, triggers and barriers; coordinate concerning changes with the prescriber.
targets.measure: Sleep timing, activation, participation in chosen roles, and feasibility of the routine.

targets.label: Act on early warning signs
targets.need: Warning signs are missed or help is delayed
targets.goal: Recognize changes early and use a shared response plan.
targets.objective: By [date], identify [target] personal warning signs and rehearse the corresponding support/contact step in [target] practice scenarios.
targets.intervention: Develop a relapse signature and written response plan with client-selected supports; rehearse help-seeking and review past episodes without blame.
targets.measure: Recognition and response-plan rehearsal; actual delay to support; symptoms and consequences of emerging episodes.

families.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
families.age: Adult core; adapt with age-specific guidance
families.context: Distinguish productive problem solving from repetitive worry and avoidance.
families.caution: Assess medical/substance contributors and comorbidity. Choose practices that increase function rather than make certainty a prerequisite.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: NICE CG113 · adult GAD and panic

targets.label: Choose action over worry
targets.need: Worry delays decisions and valued activity
targets.goal: Take meaningful action while uncertainty remains.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] planned actions per [week] despite worry, from [baseline], and record reassurance or avoidance used.
targets.intervention: Use CBT to map worry, test predictions, practice uncertainty and separate actionable problems from hypothetical worry.
targets.measure: Valued actions completed; time lost to worry; reassurance and avoidance frequency.

targets.label: Solve what is solvable
targets.need: Repeated rumination replaces practical problem solving
targets.goal: Use a bounded process for problems within the client’s control.
targets.objective: By [date], apply the agreed problem-solving sequence to [target] real-life problems and carry out one chosen step in [target] of [opportunities].
targets.intervention: Teach specific problem definition, options, a feasible action and review; use applied relaxation if it fits the chosen treatment formulation.
targets.measure: Actions taken and usefulness of decisions; time spent looping; client-rated interference.

families.name: Panic disorder and agoraphobia
families.age: Adult core
families.context: Fear of body sensations and avoided places can restrict daily life.
families.caution: New or unexplained physical symptoms need medical assessment. Interoceptive exposure requires competence and medical suitability; avoid using relaxation as a mandatory safety behavior.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: NICE CG113 · adult GAD and panic

targets.label: Regain access to places
targets.need: Panic-related avoidance narrows independence
targets.goal: Use chosen places and activities with less reliance on safety behaviors.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed situation practices per [week], from [baseline], while reducing [specified safety behavior].
targets.intervention: Use panic-focused CBT and collaboratively graded in-vivo exposure; test feared predictions and review safety behaviors.
targets.measure: Activities accessed, avoidance, safety behavior use, and learning from practice.

targets.label: Change the response to sensations
targets.need: Catastrophic interpretations of sensations escalate fear
targets.goal: Respond to panic sensations with a more flexible understanding.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] clinician-guided, medically appropriate sensation practices and describe the observed outcome versus prediction.
targets.intervention: Provide panic-cycle psychoeducation and competent interoceptive exposure within a structured CBT protocol.
targets.measure: Practice completion, catastrophic belief rating, and willingness to remain engaged despite sensations.

families.name: Social anxiety disorder
families.age: Adults and young people; use age-specific delivery
families.context: Target fear-driven avoidance rather than preferred solitude or neurodivergent communication style.
families.caution: Check actual bullying, discrimination and unsafe settings. Do not turn social goals into compelled masking or eye contact.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Participate without over-monitoring
targets.need: Fear of judgment blocks chosen participation
targets.goal: Take part in personally chosen social situations with greater freedom.
targets.objective: By [date], participate in [target] chosen social situations per [week], from [baseline], using an agreed outward-attention practice.
targets.intervention: Use social-anxiety-specific CBT, attention work, behavioral experiments and graded exposure; reduce self-focused monitoring.
targets.measure: Participation, avoidance, self-monitoring, and client-rated authenticity and freedom.

targets.label: Reduce protective routines
targets.need: Rehearsal, reassurance and post-event review consume time
targets.goal: Use fewer anxiety-maintaining safety behaviors.
targets.objective: By [date], test dropping [specified safety behavior] in [target] agreed situations and compare predicted versus observed consequences.
targets.intervention: Identify safety behaviors and post-event processing; design collaborative experiments and review evidence without reassurance rituals.
targets.measure: Safety behavior frequency, time in post-event review, and functional benefit.

families.name: Specific phobia / separation anxiety
families.age: Age-specific assessment and treatment required
families.context: These are distinct diagnoses sharing some avoidance targets. Use a disorder-specific formulation rather than treating every separation as fear.
families.caution: Rule out real danger, developmental expectations, trauma and attachment disruption. Exposure is collaborative, never forced.
families.evidence: NIMH public overview supports broad direction; use a diagnosis- and age-specific protocol for treatment detail.

targets.label: Approach a chosen feared activity
targets.need: A specific fear limits an important activity
targets.goal: Regain access to a chosen activity through manageable approach steps.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed hierarchy steps, from [baseline], documenting approach, avoidance and observed learning.
targets.intervention: Use a diagnosis-appropriate CBT exposure plan with consent/assent; adapt pace and response mode.
targets.measure: Hierarchy steps attempted and completed; participation gained; safety behaviors and distress tolerance.

targets.label: Practice supported separation
targets.need: Fear-driven separation distress limits age-appropriate participation
targets.goal: Build confidence in safe, predictable separations.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed separation practices of [duration], from [baseline], with a predictable return/support plan.
targets.intervention: Use age-appropriate CBT, caregiver coaching and gradual supported practice; assess context and developmental needs first.
targets.measure: Practice participation, duration, recovery, caregiver accommodation and sense of safety.

families.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
families.age: Adults and youth; include caregivers as appropriate
families.context: Identify overt and mental compulsions, reassurance seeking and functional cost.
families.caution: Distinguish intrusive thoughts from intent through assessment. ERP reduces rituals; it must not become repeated reassurance or a demand for anxiety to disappear.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Interrupt the ritual cycle
targets.need: Compulsions and avoidance occupy daily life
targets.goal: Choose valued action with less control by rituals.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed ERP practices per [week], from [baseline], refraining from [specified overt/mental ritual] for [agreed period].
targets.intervention: Use competent CBT with exposure and response prevention; identify hidden rituals and review learning and willingness.
targets.measure: Ritual time/frequency, response prevention, participation and optional appropriately administered OCD measure.

targets.label: Reduce accommodation
targets.need: Family reassurance and participation in rituals sustain restriction
targets.goal: Build supportive responses that do not reinforce compulsions.
targets.objective: By [date], use the agreed supportive response instead of [specified accommodation] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Collaboratively map accommodation, coach validating responses without certainty-giving and pace changes with the client and support person.
targets.measure: Accommodation frequency, support quality, distress response and function.

families.name: Body dysmorphic disorder
families.age: Adults and youth; use age-specific protocol
families.context: Appearance preoccupation, checking and avoidance interfere with daily life.
families.caution: Assess suicide risk and eating-disorder differential. Avoid reassurance about appearance or cosmetic procedures as psychotherapy goals.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Reclaim time from checking
targets.need: Appearance checking and comparison dominate routines
targets.goal: Spend more time on chosen activities and less on checking.
targets.objective: By [date], reduce [specified checking/comparison ritual] from [baseline] to [target] per [period] while completing [chosen activity].
targets.intervention: Use BDD-specific CBT including ERP, attention work and behavioral experiments; tailor mirror-related work within training.
targets.measure: Checking time/frequency, avoided activities and functional participation.

targets.label: Re-enter valued situations
targets.need: Appearance fears drive avoidance
targets.goal: Participate in chosen situations without excessive concealment or reassurance.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed situation practices per [week], from [baseline], reducing [specified safety behavior].
targets.intervention: Use BDD-specific graded exposure and response prevention; collaboratively test beliefs without arguing about appearance.
targets.measure: Participation gained, safety behavior use, distress and belief flexibility.

families.name: PTSD / trauma-related disorders
families.age: Adult core; TF-CBT and other age-specific options for youth
families.context: Clarify current threat, trauma-related avoidance, beliefs and functional goals.
families.caution: Ongoing danger requires protection and practical support. Trauma processing needs consent, appropriate training and assessment of stability; grounding alone is not full PTSD treatment.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Return to safe participation
targets.need: Trauma reminders restrict safe valued activities
targets.goal: Re-engage with safe activities the client has chosen.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed safe approach practices per [week], from [baseline], documenting avoidance and participation.
targets.intervention: Offer a competent trauma-focused treatment matched to age and preference; collaboratively address avoidance within its protocol.
targets.measure: Safe activity participation, avoidance and trauma symptoms using an appropriate measure when indicated.

targets.label: Increase choice during reminders
targets.need: Reminders lead to shutdown or loss of effective response
targets.goal: Recognize reminders and regain enough present orientation to choose a response.
targets.objective: By [date], recognize [target] personal reminder cues and use an agreed orienting/support step in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Teach trauma psychoeducation, present orientation and emotion-regulation supports; link these to, rather than substitute them for, indicated trauma-focused care.
targets.measure: Time to reorient, choice of response, functional recovery and fit of the support.

families.name: Adjustment disorders / life transitions
families.age: Across ages with developmental adaptation
families.context: Formulate a clear link between a stressor, distress and disruption of functioning.
families.caution: Assess whether depression, PTSD, grief or another condition better explains the presentation. Address ongoing adversity; distress is not automatically disorder.
families.evidence: Original transdiagnostic planning examples; APA overview supports supportive care for life stressors, not an adjustment-disorder-specific protocol.

sources.label: APA · psychotherapy for stressful life events

targets.label: Restore a workable routine
targets.need: A stressor disrupts daily roles
targets.goal: Re-establish a routine that fits the changed situation.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] chosen role/routine tasks per [week], from [baseline], using agreed supports.
targets.intervention: Use brief supportive therapy, problem solving and practical resource mapping tailored to the stressor.
targets.measure: Role participation, stressor burden, task feasibility and distress.

targets.label: Use support and boundaries
targets.need: Stress exceeds available support
targets.goal: Ask for support and set workable limits.
targets.objective: By [date], make [target] specific support requests or boundary statements and review the outcome of each.
targets.intervention: Clarify controllable needs, rehearse requests, identify practical resources and process loss/change in context.
targets.measure: Requests made, support received, boundary follow-through and client-rated agency.

families.name: Prolonged grief disorder / bereavement
families.age: Adult core; developmental and cultural assessment for youth
families.context: Support continued connection with the deceased and participation in life. Normal bereavement is not automatically a disorder.
families.caution: Establish diagnostic duration, impairment and cultural context. Assess depression, PTSD and suicide risk; do not make “moving on” or forgetting a treatment goal.
families.evidence: APA public resource supports grief-focused treatment direction; original planning examples are not a manualized protocol.

targets.label: Make space for grief and living
targets.need: Grief and avoidance prevent desired life participation
targets.goal: Hold grief while re-engaging with personally meaningful life roles.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] chosen restoration activities per [week], from [baseline], while identifying the grief/support needs that arise.
targets.intervention: Use grief-focused treatment when indicated; alternate loss-focused processing with restoration work and supported approach to avoided situations.
targets.measure: Valued participation, avoidance, grief-related impairment and personal meaning.

targets.label: Find an enduring connection
targets.need: The loss leaves a painful rupture in identity and connection
targets.goal: Develop a personally meaningful way to remember and remain connected.
targets.objective: By [date], identify and try [target] chosen remembrance/connection practices and review how each affects connection and daily function.
targets.intervention: Use grief-informed supportive work or a grief-specific protocol; explore relationship meaning, identity and community/cultural practices.
targets.measure: Client-rated connection, tolerability, identity continuity and participation.

families.name: Dissociative disorders / DID
families.age: Adult specialist pathway; do not apply adult guideline to children
families.context: Prioritize safety, cooperation, continuity and functioning. Clarify dissociation and medical/neurological differential.
families.caution: Use dissociation-specific competence and consultation. Avoid suggestive memory work, forcing disclosure, or mandating identity fusion; new speech or neurological changes need medical assessment.
families.evidence: ISSTD 2011 adult specialist consensus guideline; evidence and training needs differ from well-established disorder-specific CBT protocols. Objectives are original.

sources.label: ISSTD · adult DID guidelines (2011 specialist consensus)

targets.label: Increase present orientation
targets.need: Dissociation interrupts participation or safety
targets.goal: Notice dissociative shifts and regain orientation using accessible supports.
targets.objective: By [date], recognize [target] personally useful early cues and use [chosen orienting support] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Use phase-oriented stabilization, collaborative psychoeducation and individualized present-orientation practice; assess what worsens symptoms.
targets.measure: Time lost, recovery/orientation, support use and safe participation; self-report interpreted in context.

targets.label: Improve continuity and cooperation
targets.need: Memory gaps or conflicting responses disrupt daily roles
targets.goal: Increase continuity and internal cooperation around shared daily needs.
targets.objective: By [date], use an agreed non-coercive continuity aid for [chosen task] on [target] days per [week], from [baseline], and review barriers safely.
targets.intervention: Support internal communication and shared safety agreements within specialist phase-oriented treatment; use neutral logs or cues when acceptable.
targets.measure: Task continuity, gaps and consequences, internal conflict, agency and safety.

families.name: Borderline personality disorder
families.age: Adult core; adolescent formulation needs developmental expertise
families.context: Choose a coherent treatment frame and hierarchy. Link emotion, relationship and safety targets to client priorities.
families.caution: DBT-informed skills are not equivalent to comprehensive DBT. Risk and therapy-interfering behaviors require a shared hierarchy, continuity and a specific response plan.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Respond safely to intense emotion
targets.need: Intense affect prompts harmful or destabilizing responses
targets.goal: Use safer responses that preserve relationships and personal goals.
targets.objective: By [date], use an agreed alternative response in [target] of [high-intensity episodes], from [baseline], with chain review of barriers.
targets.intervention: Use a structured BPD treatment within competence; teach and rehearse relevant DBT skills, conduct chain analysis and prioritize safety targets.
targets.measure: Harmful-response frequency/severity, alternative response use, recovery and valued functioning.

targets.label: Communicate needs and repair
targets.need: Relationship rupture interrupts trust and treatment
targets.goal: Express needs and repair conflict with greater consistency.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed request/boundary/repair sequence] in [target] interactions per [period], from [baseline], and review the effect.
targets.intervention: Use the agreed treatment frame to practice interpersonal effectiveness, validate distress, examine assumptions and maintain consistent boundaries.
targets.measure: Requests, repairs, ruptures, treatment engagement and client-rated relationship stability.

families.name: Other personality / enduring relational patterns
families.age: Adults; avoid premature personality labeling in youth
families.context: Formulate enduring patterns and the function they serve; diagnosis alone does not select a treatment.
families.caution: Do not generalize BPD recommendations to every personality disorder. Assess coercion, violence, trauma and neurodevelopmental explanations; use specialist formulation as needed.
families.evidence: Original transdiagnostic examples informed by a public APA overview; select a disorder-specific specialist formulation and treatment.

targets.label: Increase flexibility in relationships
targets.need: Rigid expectations or protective strategies create repeated conflict
targets.goal: Choose responses that better match current relationship goals.
targets.objective: By [date], identify [target] recurring interaction patterns and test an alternative response in [target] agreed situations.
targets.intervention: Use collaborative relational formulation and structured behavioral experiments consistent with the chosen therapy model.
targets.measure: Pattern recognition, alternative responses, consequences and relationship function.

targets.label: Protect boundaries and agency
targets.need: Difficulty with limits or trust disrupts chosen roles
targets.goal: Set and maintain boundaries that support autonomy and connection.
targets.objective: By [date], communicate [target] specific boundaries or preferences and review follow-through and safety after each.
targets.intervention: Use supportive/relational psychotherapy, rehearsal and review of expectations and consequences; refer when specialist treatment is indicated.
targets.measure: Boundary enactment, felt agency, conflict impact and support quality.

families.name: Schizophrenia spectrum / psychotic disorders
families.age: Adult core; youth needs an early-intervention specialist pathway
families.context: Focus on distress, recovery and chosen roles, alongside coordinated psychiatric care.
families.caution: New psychosis, dangerous command experiences, marked deterioration or catatonia needs urgent assessment. Do not confront beliefs or affirm delusional content as established fact.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Reduce interference from experiences
targets.need: Voices or unusual experiences interrupt daily life
targets.goal: Respond in ways that reduce distress and protect chosen activities.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed coping response] in [target] of [distressing episodes], from [baseline], and document its effect on participation.
targets.intervention: Use competent CBT for psychosis: explore meaning and context collaboratively, test coping strategies and support recovery without arguing about beliefs.
targets.measure: Distress, interference, coping usefulness, safety and role participation.

targets.label: Strengthen recovery support
targets.need: Symptoms and practical barriers interrupt routines and support
targets.goal: Maintain a recovery routine and access help early.
targets.objective: By [date], carry out [target] chosen recovery/support steps per [week], from [baseline], and rehearse the early-warning response.
targets.intervention: Use recovery planning, family intervention where appropriate and consented, and coordinated support for chosen social/vocational goals.
targets.measure: Support access, routine participation, early-warning response and client-defined recovery.

families.name: ADHD
families.age: Adults and youth; developmental adaptation
families.context: Target task access and functioning rather than effort or compliance. Assess environmental barriers and co-occurring needs.
families.caution: Coordinate assessment and medication questions with appropriate clinicians. Supports should be feasible; reward systems are not a substitute for access or skills.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Make tasks easier to start
targets.need: Initiation and working-memory load block valued tasks
targets.goal: Start chosen tasks using reliable external supports.
targets.objective: By [date], start [chosen task] within [agreed interval] using [support] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Use ADHD-focused skills work and environmental modification: break tasks into visible steps, externalize cues and rehearse task launch.
targets.measure: Start latency, opportunities completed with supports, burden and independence chosen by the client.

targets.label: Finish and recover from interruption
targets.need: Interruptions and sequencing difficulties derail completion
targets.goal: Complete or deliberately reschedule tasks with less avoidable disruption.
targets.objective: By [date], use an agreed next-step/restart cue in [target] of [task interruptions], from [baseline], and complete the planned task segment.
targets.intervention: Teach planning and restart strategies, practice in real routines and adapt caregiver support when appropriate.
targets.measure: Restart success, completed segments, missed commitments and support burden.

families.name: Autism
families.age: Adults and youth with age-appropriate adaptations
families.context: Target access, autonomy, communication and co-occurring distress. Autistic traits are not themselves defects to eliminate.
families.caution: Do not set forced eye contact, masking or suppression of harmless regulation as goals. Examine overload, pain, communication mismatch and coercion before labeling behavior.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: NICE CG170 · autistic children and adolescents

targets.label: Increase communication and choice
targets.need: Communication mismatch limits participation and assent
targets.goal: Express preferences and influence decisions through a reliable preferred mode.
targets.objective: By [date], communicate a choice, refusal or request using [preferred mode] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], with agreed partner supports.
targets.intervention: Use accessible psychotherapy, visual/communication supports and partner coaching; coordinate with SLP/AAC services when needed.
targets.measure: Choices acknowledged, requests understood, ability to refuse and client-rated agency; partner responsiveness.

targets.label: Reduce overload and support recovery
targets.need: Sensory or demand overload disrupts wellbeing
targets.goal: Recognize load and obtain supports before or during overload.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed signal/support] in [target] of [overload opportunities], from [baseline], with a jointly agreed recovery routine.
targets.intervention: Map sensory and demand load, adapt the environment and collaboratively rehearse recovery and transition supports.
targets.measure: Overload frequency/duration, recovery time, support availability and participation without masking demands.

families.name: Intellectual disability / adaptive support needs
families.age: Across ages; match developmental and communication needs
families.context: Adapt psychotherapy to comprehension, communication and daily support needs. Involve the person directly.
families.caution: Assess pain, illness, environment and unmet communication needs. Caregiver goals must not replace the person’s preferences or supported assent.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: NICE NG11 · learning disability and behavior that challenges

targets.label: Support everyday decision making
targets.need: Information or response barriers limit choice
targets.goal: Make meaningful choices with the right support.
targets.objective: By [date], make and communicate [target] everyday choices per [period], from [baseline], with [specified support] and a genuine refusal option.
targets.intervention: Use concrete language, visual options, rehearsal and teach-back; coach supporters to allow processing time and honor choices.
targets.measure: Choices offered and honored, understanding, support level and personal agency.

targets.label: Understand distress in context
targets.need: Distress is interpreted without attention to function or health
targets.goal: Identify unmet needs and use accessible ways to seek support.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed help/break/need signal] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], while supporters record context and response.
targets.intervention: Use functional assessment, communication supports and caregiver coaching; coordinate medical review and positive support planning.
targets.measure: Needs identified, partner response, distress duration and access to preferred activities.

families.name: ODD / conduct and disruptive behavior disorders
families.age: Children and adolescents; family and systems involvement
families.context: Separate skill, communication and access barriers from learned interaction patterns. Assess safety and context.
families.caution: Aggression, abuse and coercion need an explicit safety response. Avoid humiliation, deprivation of essential supports, or making the child responsible for adult conflict.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: NICE CG158 · child and adolescent conduct disorders

targets.label: Change escalation patterns
targets.need: Recurring demand-conflict cycles disrupt safety and relationships
targets.goal: Replace escalation with a clear, supported response sequence.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed pause/request/return sequence] in [target] of [conflict opportunities], from [baseline], with a coordinated adult response.
targets.intervention: Use age-appropriate evidence-based parent/family intervention; map antecedents and consequences, coach clear directions and reinforce specific alternative behaviors.
targets.measure: Escalation frequency/severity, adult consistency, alternative behavior and relationship repair.

targets.label: Build task follow-through
targets.need: Tasks are poorly matched, inconsistently prompted or repeatedly avoided
targets.goal: Complete feasible tasks with predictable support and accountability.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [chosen task segment] with [agreed support] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Use behavioral parent training and joint problem solving; check skill/capacity first, define a feasible task and rehearse consistent contingencies.
targets.measure: Task completion, prompts needed, access barriers and conflict cost.

families.name: Anger / impulse-control presentations
families.age: Across ages after differential assessment
families.context: A shared target menu for anger and impulsive aggression; it does not establish intermittent explosive disorder.
families.caution: Assess violence risk, substance use, mania, trauma, neurodevelopment and coercive control. Safety planning must be specific to the context.
families.evidence: Original transdiagnostic examples; child conduct and BPD sources inform adjacent skills approaches, not an IED-specific treatment protocol.

sources.label: NICE CG158 · child and adolescent conduct disorders

targets.label: Interrupt escalation
targets.need: Rising activation leads to harmful actions
targets.goal: Recognize escalation and use a safer next action.
targets.objective: By [date], use [agreed exit/pause/help sequence] in [target] of [escalations], from [baseline], documenting safety and return to discussion.
targets.intervention: Use formulation-based CBT/skills practice, chain analysis, behavioral rehearsal and a context-specific safety plan.
targets.measure: Aggression frequency/severity, early cue recognition, safer actions and impact on others.

targets.label: Repair and solve the trigger
targets.need: Conflict recurs without accountability or problem solving
targets.goal: Take responsibility and address the problem after regulation.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [agreed accountability/repair/problem-solving steps] following [target] of [eligible conflicts], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Rehearse non-coercive repair, perspective taking and concrete problem solving; involve caregivers or systems when appropriate and safe.
targets.measure: Repairs completed, recurrence, responsibility taken and whether others feel safe.

families.name: Substance use disorders
families.age: Adult core; adolescent treatment needs age-specific care
families.context: Separate alcohol, opioid, stimulant, cannabis and other substances in assessment. Agree on abstinence or harm-reduction goals and coordinate indicated medical treatment.
families.caution: Assess intoxication, overdose and withdrawal risk. Alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal can require medical care; psychotherapy does not replace medications or withdrawal management.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Move toward a chosen change
targets.need: Use conflicts with health, roles or personal priorities
targets.goal: Reduce substance-related harm and move toward the agreed use goal.
targets.objective: By [date], change [substance/use pattern or harm indicator] from [baseline] to [target] per [period], reviewed collaboratively without punitive interpretation.
targets.intervention: Use motivational interviewing and a substance-specific treatment plan; select indicated CBT, contingency management or other supported care and coordinate medical treatment.
targets.measure: Use pattern, harm events, valued functioning and agreed objective information where clinically appropriate.

targets.label: Prepare for high-risk situations
targets.need: Craving and predictable triggers undermine change
targets.goal: Use a workable response and access support during high-risk situations.
targets.objective: By [date], rehearse [target] trigger-response plans and use [chosen support/response] in [target] of [high-risk opportunities], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Use functional analysis, coping practice and relapse prevention; review recurrence as information and address access to recovery support and overdose prevention.
targets.measure: Response-plan use, cravings, recurrence pattern, help access and consequences.

families.name: Anorexia nervosa / restrictive eating
families.age: Adults and youth; treatment selection depends on age and medical status
families.context: Use an eating-disorder specialist pathway with medical and nutritional collaboration. Psychotherapy targets support the team’s individualized recovery plan.
families.caution: Medical instability, rapid deterioration or inability to maintain intake needs timely medical assessment. Do not set generic weight targets or use this menu as nutritional prescribing.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Engage with the recovery plan
targets.need: Restriction and fear interfere with the team’s recovery plan
targets.goal: Participate in individualized eating-disorder care with support.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] of [team-defined recovery behaviors], from [baseline], documenting barriers and agreed support.
targets.intervention: Use an indicated age-appropriate eating-disorder treatment; coordinate medical/nutrition monitoring and family-based care when appropriate.
targets.measure: Team-defined nutritional/medical indicators, recovery behavior, participation and access barriers.

targets.label: Reduce eating-disorder interference
targets.need: Rigid rules and fear narrow daily life
targets.goal: Increase flexible participation in recovery-consistent activities.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed specialist-guided behavioral experiments involving [rule/avoided recovery activity], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Within the selected eating-disorder protocol, address maintaining beliefs, avoidance and identity/values beyond the disorder.
targets.measure: Rule interference, avoided activities, distress, functional participation and medical status.

families.name: Bulimia nervosa / binge-eating disorder
families.age: Adults and youth; diagnosis- and age-specific care
families.context: These are distinct diagnoses. Select the relevant binge, compensatory behavior and eating-pattern targets.
families.caution: Purging can create medical risk. Do not make weight loss a routine binge-eating treatment goal; distinguish dieting from the treatment team’s regular-eating plan.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Interrupt the binge / compensatory cycle
targets.need: Binge episodes or compensatory behaviors disrupt health and function
targets.goal: Reduce the maintaining cycle and regain flexibility around eating.
targets.objective: By [date], change [defined binge/compensatory behavior] from [baseline] to [target] per [period], with medical monitoring when indicated.
targets.intervention: Use indicated eating-disorder-focused CBT/guided self-help or age-appropriate family treatment; map maintaining cycles and address relevant triggers.
targets.measure: Episode frequency, compensatory behaviors, distress, function and medical status.

targets.label: Support a regular eating plan
targets.need: Restriction and irregular eating maintain the cycle
targets.goal: Follow a collaboratively established recovery eating pattern.
targets.objective: By [date], carry out [team-agreed eating-pattern step] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], and review barriers.
targets.intervention: Support the specialist/nutrition team’s individualized plan within an eating-disorder protocol; address shame, rules and avoidance.
targets.measure: Pattern consistency, restriction, binge urges, flexibility and participation.

families.name: ARFID / avoidant-restrictive food intake
families.age: Across ages; specialist feeding/eating assessment
families.context: Identify sensory sensitivity, feared consequences and low interest separately. Assess nutritional and functional consequences.
families.caution: Coordinate medical, nutrition and feeding/SLP/OT assessment as indicated. Rule out swallowing problems and allergy; no forced feeding or unsafe exposure.
families.evidence: NIMH public overview describes ARFID; these original access targets are adjuncts, not an ARFID treatment protocol.

targets.label: Increase safe food participation
targets.need: Avoidance restricts adequate intake or participation
targets.goal: Expand safe, tolerable participation in the specialist-agreed eating plan.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed safe food/meal participation practices, from [baseline], at a tolerable pace.
targets.intervention: Support an ARFID-specific specialist plan, matching practice to the maintaining pathway and sensory/communication needs.
targets.measure: Intake adequacy monitored by the team, participation, variety where relevant, and tolerability.

targets.label: Communicate eating support needs
targets.need: Pressure and misunderstood needs worsen avoidance
targets.goal: Access eating supports without coercion.
targets.objective: By [date], communicate [specified food/setting/support need] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], with an agreed partner response.
targets.intervention: Use collaborative problem solving, predictable routines and partner coaching alongside specialist feeding/eating treatment.
targets.measure: Needs communicated and honored, pressure reduced, participation and team-defined nutritional status.

families.name: Insomnia disorder
families.age: Adult core; use pediatric sleep guidance for minors
families.context: Differentiate chronic insomnia from circadian problems, sleep apnea, parasomnia and insufficient sleep opportunity.
families.caution: CBT-I requires training. Sleep-restriction components need clinical screening and monitoring, especially with bipolar disorder, seizures or safety-sensitive work.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

sources.label: VA/DoD · chronic insomnia and sleep apnea

targets.label: Improve sleep-related functioning
targets.need: Persistent insomnia impairs daytime life
targets.goal: Improve sleep and daytime functioning with an individualized plan.
targets.objective: By [date], change [agreed sleep/daytime indicator] from [baseline] to [target], recorded over [period] in a sleep diary.
targets.intervention: Use competent CBT-I or refer; tailor stimulus control, sleep scheduling and cognitive work after clinical assessment.
targets.measure: Sleep diary indicators, daytime function and an appropriately administered insomnia measure.

targets.label: Reduce struggle around sleep
targets.need: Sleep effort and rigid predictions increase interference
targets.goal: Use a more flexible response to wakefulness within the CBT-I plan.
targets.objective: By [date], follow [agreed CBT-I response to wakefulness] in [target] of [opportunities], from [baseline], and review daytime safety.
targets.intervention: Use CBT-I cognitive/behavioral work to address sleep effort and unhelpful beliefs; screen for other sleep disorders and coordinate care.
targets.measure: Response use, sleep effort, daytime impairment and safety.

families.name: Somatic symptom / illness anxiety presentations
families.age: Adult core; age-specific adaptation
families.context: Symptoms are real experiences. Differentiate medical conditions, disproportionate health worry and repeated checking; psychological and medical care can coexist.
families.caution: New or worsening symptoms need appropriate medical assessment. Avoid dismissing symptoms as “just anxiety” or withholding medically indicated evaluation.
families.evidence: APA public overview supports broad psychotherapy direction. Separate illness-anxiety formulation and original objectives require individual clinical judgment.

sources.label: American Psychiatric Association · somatic symptom disorder

targets.label: Rebuild life around symptoms
targets.need: Symptoms and health worry restrict chosen activities
targets.goal: Improve participation while receiving appropriate medical care.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [target] agreed activities per [week], from [baseline], using the coordinated medical and psychological plan.
targets.intervention: Use formulation-based CBT/supportive care and paced participation; coordinate consistent medical follow-up and address illness beliefs without dismissal.
targets.measure: Function, symptom burden, health-worry interference and coordination.

targets.label: Reduce repetitive checking
targets.need: Reassurance/checking provides only brief relief
targets.goal: Use an agreed response to health worry with less repetitive checking.
targets.objective: By [date], reduce [specified non-indicated checking/reassurance behavior] from [baseline] to [target] per [period], preserving indicated medical care.
targets.intervention: Collaboratively map the worry-checking cycle, test alternatives and agree on how to respond to genuine medical changes.
targets.measure: Checking time, reassurance frequency, meaningful activity and appropriate medical engagement.

families.name: Chronic pain / health-related adjustment
families.age: Adult core; medical coordination
families.context: An adjunct psychotherapy menu for functioning with chronic pain or illness; pain is not itself a psychiatric diagnosis.
families.caution: NICE NG193 distinguishes chronic primary from secondary pain. Treat the actual medical condition; do not imply symptoms are imagined or increase activity against medical restrictions.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Increase sustainable participation
targets.need: Pain and boom-bust activity restrict daily roles
targets.goal: Participate in chosen activities at a sustainable pace.
targets.objective: By [date], complete [chosen activity] at [agreed level] on [target] days per [period], from [baseline], within medical limits.
targets.intervention: Use indicated pain-focused CBT or ACT, pacing and values-based planning alongside medical care; review load and recovery.
targets.measure: Activity sustainability, role participation, interference and recovery cost.

targets.label: Respond flexibly to flare-ups
targets.need: Flare-ups disrupt coping and continuity
targets.goal: Use a workable flare-up plan that preserves agency and care access.
targets.objective: By [date], apply [agreed flare-up/support sequence] in [target] of [episodes], from [baseline], and review what was helpful.
targets.intervention: Map early cues, flexible activity options, support needs and appropriate medical contact; rehearse coping without invalidating symptoms.
targets.measure: Plan use, interference, help access and ability to resume chosen routines.

families.name: Neurocognitive disorders / dementia
families.age: Adults; medical/neuropsychological assessment and caregiver collaboration
families.context: Target supported participation, distress and caregiver response. Restoration goals must match the condition and capacity.
families.caution: Sudden confusion or decline needs assessment for delirium/medical causes. Obtain appropriate consent and supported participation; distinguish caregiver convenience from the person’s wellbeing.
families.evidence: Guideline-informed treatment direction; objectives are original examples.

targets.label: Maintain supported participation
targets.need: Cognitive changes interrupt familiar meaningful routines
targets.goal: Sustain meaningful participation with appropriate support.
targets.objective: By [date], participate in [chosen familiar activity] with [agreed cues/support] on [target] days per [period], from [baseline].
targets.intervention: Use person-centered supportive work, environmental cues and caregiver coaching; coordinate OT/medical services and adapt expectations over time.
targets.measure: Participation, comfort, cue/support level and personal preference.

targets.label: Respond to distress and unmet needs
targets.need: Distress is misunderstood or escalates during care
targets.goal: Identify needs and reduce avoidable distress during support.
targets.objective: By [date], supporters use [agreed context/need/response sequence] in [target] of [distress episodes], from [baseline], documenting the result.
targets.intervention: Assess pain, illness, overload and communication barriers; coach calm, validating responses and adapt routines/environment.
targets.measure: Distress frequency/duration, unmet needs identified, response fit and caregiver burden.
